messages:
suresh: FYI — AcmeCorp (Dedicated) is hitting tail latency when a few huge requests land together. They want a recommended token-budget + queue policy so other tenants on the pool don't starve. Can we propose config + rollout plan?

rachel: quick thought: prefer token-based batch formation for this customer (not request-count). Set per-request token_budget so a single long prompt can't blow out a batch. Also put a max_queue_tokens cap to bound queue depth.

mike: +1. From infra side we need both soft and hard queue timeouts so very old requests get forced through instead of never materializing. Also KV cache behavior matters — if big requests thrash the cache we pay kernel-switch penalties.

lia: customer requirement: p95 < 250ms under their steady 8k qps profile, occasional spikes to 16k qps for short windows. They asked specifically for "no single customer request causing >1s p99". Can the config guarantee that?

rachel: guarantees are hard w/o more isolation, but we can tighten QoS. Proposal (start canary):

```yaml
# per-customer QoS for Dedicated pool "acme-dedicated-1"
pool: acme-dedicated-1
max_concurrent_batches: 12               # limit batch concurrency on pool
token_budget_per_request: 2048           # cap per-request tokens considered for batch
max_queue_tokens: 32768                  # total tokens allowed in queue
queue_soft_timeout_ms: 150               # try to form batch within this ms
queue_hard_timeout_ms: 350               # force through after this ms
early_cutoff_pct: 0.6                    # cut batch when 60% token budget reached to lower latency
kv_cache_priority: true                  # prefer keeping KV cache hot for recent sessions
prefer_small_token_kernel_threshold: 128 # choose fast attention kernel for short sequences
```

rachel: Notes: early_cutoff_pct trades throughput for tail latency. token_budget_per_request prevents single huge request from becoming batch killer. kv_cache_priority lets us favor allocations that preserve hot KV pages for streaming chat workloads.

mike: I'll add autoscaling guardrails and metric hooks. Instrument these metrics for the canary: `batch_formation_time_ms`, `batch_tokens`, `kernel_switches`, `kv_miss_rate`, `p95_latency_ms`, `p99_latency_ms`, `queue_length_tokens`.

mike: Suggested rollout plan: canary on 5% of Acme traffic for 2 hours -> if p95 < 300ms and kv_miss_rate doesn't spike > 2x, ramp to 25% for 4 hours -> then full. Add automatic rollback if p99 > 750ms for 10m.

ops-bot: deploy-plan: canary acme-qos-v1 -> 2025-07-10T18:00:00Z, rollback-window=30m, alert-channel=#eng-runtime.

lia: I'll send this to the customer as a proposed config. They also asked about kernel selection: can we guarantee the fast kernel will be used for short sequences?

rachel: kernel selection is runtime-driven: short sequences + quantized weights => use fast attention kernel. We'll add a profiling pass during canary: collect `seq_len_histogram` and `kernel_choice_ratio`. If kernel switches increase, we may need separate small/large device pools or tweak `prefer_small_token_kernel_threshold`.

suresh: one operational concern: if the pool already has cross-tenant workloads, do we need per-customer queue isolation? Otherwise their `max_queue_tokens` could be affected by noisy neighbors.
rachel: good call — for Dedicated we should be able to provide per-customer logical queues inside the pool. If not, we'll enforce per-tenant max in the router before entering the pool.

mike: I'll draft the router patch: simple token-accounting window (sliding 1s) that rejects/defers requests exceeding tenant_token_rate. Quick pseudocode: 

```
# pseudo
if tenant.queue_tokens + req.tokens > tenant.max_queue_tokens:
  if req.is_urgent: force_through_with_penalty()
  else: return 429 with Retry-After
else:
  enqueue(req)
```

lia: Can you add expected customer-facing error messaging? They prefer graceful 429 + suggested token truncation tips for SDK users.

rachel: yup — SDK client helper will include `suggested_truncation=1024` and `recommended_batching=true` in the 429 payload.

mike: action items: 1) infra implement queue guard + metrics (owner: mike) 2) runtime apply QoS config + kernel telemetry (owner: rachel) 3) ops schedule canary and alerts (owner: ops-bot) 4) AM send proposal and firmware (owner: lia). I'll create a PR with the config and tests.

suresh: thanks — please paste PR when ready. :thumbsup:
